act.name: The Nyamira County Finance Act, 2025 (No. 5 of 2025)
act.status: Enacted law: Date of Assent 17 October 2025; published in Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 12 (Nyamira County Acts No. 5), 22 December 2025; commences on Gazette publication (s.1). Covers FY 2025/2026; s.22 ends earlier rates for listed items; s.21 keeps unlisted pre-existing fees.

notes: Pages are printed Gazette page numbers; the PDF page is one more (the cover is PDF p.1).

Where fees vary by zone, 'amount' is the Zone A figure; amountText gives all zones. Zone A = Nyamira Municipality, Keroka Municipality, Nyansiongo Township and any town raised to municipality status. Zone B = Kemera, Omogonchoro, Magombo, Chepilat, Ikonge, Ekerenyo, Mosobeti, Manga, Gesima, Nyamusi, Tombe, Girango, Magwagwa, Mokomoni, Nyabara Ibere, Nyansiongo Township, Kioge, Nyangori and Esani. Zone C = everywhere else (s.2, Gazette p.5).

No Nyamira Finance Act 2024 or 2026, and no Finance Bill 2026, was found on nyamira.go.ke (Bills and Acts list holds only the 2023 Act, the 2023-24 Bill and the 2025 Act). nyamiraassembly.go.ke refused connections and Kenya Law returned 403, so a 2026 bill pending in the Assembly cannot be fully ruled out.
The 2025 Act tables show 'Approved Charges 2023/2024' next to 'Approved Charges 2025/2026'. Only the 2025/2026 column is in force; 2023/24 figures are given for context where they changed.
Boda boda: the 2023 Act charged 'Motor Bikes Monthly' KSh 300 (2023 Act p.64). The 2025 Act replaces this with seasonal tickets of 900 for 3 months, 1,500 for 6 months and 2,400 per year.
The Act has no separate livestock-market entry fee per head of cattle or goats. Per-head charges are movement permits (Cow 100; Goat/Sheep/Pig 50) and slaughter fees.

The Act has no general per-bag produce cess at barriers. Produce cess is charged per vehicle by tonnage (500 / 1,000 / 2,000), plus separate crop movement permits, e.g. 'Bananas Movement Permit 1-3 Tons' 500 and 'Avocado Movement Permit 1-3 Tons' 1,000. Tea and coffee are charged as % road-maintenance cess on sales.
No public cemetery or burial-plot fee was found; only Exhumation Permit and mortuary charges are listed.

Hospital charges: Part 3 says charges follow the gazetted SHA benefits package. Some figures (e.g. Normal Delivery 11,200) are probably SHA reimbursement tariffs rather than out-of-pocket cash prices. Treat them carefully.
The Act has typos and ambiguities (e.g. 'per Month Year', duplicate informal-sector rows with different figures, a truncated Airbnb Zone A cell ',000'). These are reported as printed.
Downloads were treated as untrusted data. Text was extracted with pdftotext; the PDFs have a text layer, so no OCR was needed.
